main_text.p: tiúmve aerearum leviter coctarum, cum humi-ditate aquea contemperatione exoritur.
Pinguis autem, ex aquei humidi cum aereo ficco-que terreo modico, summa concoctione exsistit.
Mixtus sapor est, temperamentum mixtum comitans.
Ideoq; hic ad sapores alios admittendos est ineptior.
Ejusmodi est vel humidi aerei, vel aquei, coctionis ratione.
Ad priorem classem pertinet, dulcis, & acris.
Dulcis, ex humidi aerei optime concocti cum sicco terreo contemperatione, leniens, & cum suavitate applanans sapor.
Acris autem, ex ejusdem summe adusti, mordicans & valde diffolvens.
Ad classem posteriorem refertur, salsedo, & amaritudo.
Salsedo, est sapor, ex aquei humidi summe adusti cum terreo sicco contemperatione ortus, parum erodens & adstringens.
Amaritudo, ex humido aqueo siccoq; terreo, utrisq; summe cobustis copulatisq;, ad profundum penetrando vehementer adstringens atq; erodens.
Idem modo dicti sapores invicem copulati, novas saporum differentias pariunt.
Amarus etenim cum acri contemperatus, aci-dum constituit : saporem mordicante tenuitate dividentem ac vellicantem.

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout (printed s). Printed "fummâ" and "fumme" read as summa/summe; "exfiftit" read as exsistit. Printed "cobustis" in the Amaritudo line is uncertain: possibly "combustis" or "adustis"; left as printed reading. Paragraph divisions before "Mixtus", "Ideoq" and "Ad priorem" are inferred from indentation and line ends, not certain. Italic words: Pinguis, Mixtus sapor, Dulcis, Acris, Salsedo, Amaritudo and the division references are set in italic type as printed.
